C0.quote: Motivated by recent work in computational social choice, we extend the metric distortion framework
C0.note: Borderline. The model is clustering of agents from their rankings and is framed as representative election and voting. Coded eligible because algorithms aggregate agents' rankings into a collective choice of centers.

C1.quote: we give two deterministic polynomial time algorithms for k-center
C1.note: Results are algorithms plus lower bounds on distortion and queries. AL and WD fit about equally, so AL is chosen as listed first.

C2.1.quote: An ordinal preference profile P is then just the collection of the points’ rankings

C2.2.quote: each point x ∈ X provides a ranking πx : [n] → X
C2.2.note: The input is a ranking per agent. Limited cardinal distance queries are an additional resource of the algorithm, not a submitted input.

C2.3.quote: each point x ∈ X provides a ranking πx : [n] → X that is consistent with d
C2.3.note: The underlying metric d (agent distances) is the held attitude.

C2.4.quote: Each point x ∈ X reports a ranking πx that is consistent with the distances d.
C2.4.note: Rankings P and distances d have separate notation. The ranking is only required to be consistent with d. IDS also fits, but DIST is listed first.

C3.1.note: No analysis considers misreporting. Rankings are always consistent with d.

C3.2.quote: Each point x ∈ X reports a ranking πx that is consistent with the distances d.
C3.2.note: Stated only as a consistency requirement, not as sincerity.

C3.3.note: No reason is given for consistent reporting.

C4.1.quote: ranking that is consistent with d in the sense that
C4.1.note: Costs and distortion are defined via the metric d, and rankings are derived from d.

C5.1.quote: We say that an algorithm A achieves distortion D with constant
C5.1.note: Distortion is the main evaluation criterion.

C5.2.quote: let C ∗ (d) be a solution (set of centers) of minimal cost
C5.2.note: Cost and distortion are evaluated on the underlying metric d, which is defined separately from the rankings.

VOT.quote_behav: Each point x ∈ X reports a ranking πx that is consistent with the distances d.
VOT.note: Agents (points) report fixed rankings consistent with d. Counted as present because they submit rankings.

CAN.note: Centers are chosen from the agents and are not acting agents.

DES.note: The algorithm designer's objective is not modelled as an agent.

C9.1.note: The introduction mentions representative election only as motivation. No claims about which rule to use or about voter well-being were found.

C10.1.note: No explicit procedural reading is stated.
